----Appellant Versus Suresh Kumar son of Shri Sabu Lal Sindhi, Sitala Kirana, Baniyon Ka Talab,
Post-Tilswa, Mahadev, P.S. Bijoliya, District Bhilwara.
----Respondent For Appellant(s) : Mr. Mahipal Bishnoi, Pp.

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Naresh Singh
on behalf of Mr. Rakesh Arora.
Hon'Ble Mr. Justice G.R. Moolchandani Judgment 06/08/2019

This Criminal Appeal is directed against the order/judgment dated 10th February, 2004, passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mandalgarh, Bhilwara in connection with Criminal Case No. 288/1996 : State of Rajasthan Vs. Suresh Kumar S/o Sabu Lal whereby, Trial Court has acquitted the accused person for the offence punishable under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Alteration Act.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mandalgarh, Bhilwara
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: State of Rajasthan Vs. Suresh Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The factual matrix discloses that on 4th June, 1996, adulterative edible coriander was seized while same was being vend by accused respondent and upon a complaint, trial for the offence punishable under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was launched against the accused person.

The Court below did find that compliance of Rule 13(2) of the Act was (2 of 3) [CRLA-49/2005] not meticulously made, since the receipt demonstrating dispatch of the notice sent under Section 13(2)
of the Act was lacking proper address on the receipt and sheer name of accused- respondent was mentioned instead of his complete address so, the Court below delivered the judgment acquitting the accused respondent.
Aggrieved against the order impugned, appellant State has assailed the same by way of instant appeal.
Heard the arguments.

Learned counsel representing appellant State has contended that the Court below has ignored Ex./16 facsimile of the notice, which contains complete address of the accused respondent as such,
compliance of Section 13(2) of the Act was enough but ignoring this aspect, learned Court below has acquitted the accused person.

The offence has properly been proved, so respondent ought to have been convicted, hence appeal be allowed and the impugned order be reversed and respondent Suresh Kumar be convicted for the offence punishable under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

On the contrary, learned counsel representing respondent accused has urged that compliance of mandatory provision enshrined under Section 13(2) of PFA Act has not been made meticulously and Ex/17 does not indicate as to on which address and to whom, alleged notice was forwarded, so mandatory provision of the PFA Act has not been adhered too, therefore, there is no flaw or infirmity in the order impugned, appeal lacks merit, so it be dismissed.
Heard and perused the record thoroughly and scanned the order impugned.

It evinces from the record that compliance of (3 of 3) [CRLA-49/2005] Section 13(2) of the Act has not been made properly because the postal receipt (Ex/17) does has got name of accused respondent Suresh Kumar but it lacks complete address, which goes to suggests that it is not manifest as to on what address,
the said mandatory notice prescribed was forwarded.

Learned Court below, while appreciating this mandatory provision has rightly concluded that service of mandatory notice prescribed under Section 13(2) of the Act has not been made properly and adequately.
Had it been served properly upon the accused respondent, surely, he would have exercised his right to get the sample re-tested.
Learned Court below, while observing this deficiency has legitimately and rightly acquitted the accused respondent.
For the reasons deliberated and delineated hereinbefore, there appears no cause to interfere with the findings of the Court below.
Resultantly, appeal being bereft of merit, is dismissed.
Record of the Trial Court be transmitted back with a copy of this judgment.

(G.R. MOOLCHANDANI),J H8-Mohan/-
